Tools

Part of the guidelines for translating ancient texts (translation-guidelines.md), split out of it on 2026-10-21 to keep the core file lean. Section number §10, as in the guidelines.

10. Tools (tools/)

Script What Usage
ebl_fetch.py Downloads an eBL corpus chapter and builds reading-edition.md, glossary.md, manuscripts.md, bibliography.md, chapter.atf. Caches in _raw/. python3 -I tools/ebl_fetch.py --list · python3 -I tools/ebl_fetch.py L 1 4 "Standard Babylonian" XI sources/eBL/Gilgamesh-SB-XI
etcsl2md.py ETCSL TEI XML → Markdown (Unicode transliteration, subscript indices). python3 -I tools/etcsl2md.py <c-or-t.xml> <out.md> [url]
cdl2md.py ORACC CDL JSON (from a project zip) → Markdown with lemmatization. python3 -I tools/cdl2md.py <zip> <member> <out.md> <title> <url>
dfhg2md.py DFHG API JSON (Greek fragments) → Markdown. python3 -I tools/dfhg2md.py <in.json> <out.md> <title> <api-url> [frags]

More tools (2026-10-16):

  • check_bible_quotes.py: checks every backticked, vocalized Bible quotation that is followed by a reference against תנך-מנוקד/. It normalizes Unicode, allows prefixes and quotations that run on into the next verses, and defaults to Genesis. python3 -I tools/check_bible_quotes.py <files…>; --show בראשית "ח כא" prints a verse. Run it before finishing any project. Note: the Psalms and Proverbs files use a hyphen-minus for maqaf, so keep the - in quotations from them.
  • ebl_fetch.py (fixed 2026-10-16): notes are now taken from the JSON (the ATF omits many), and range lines (66-67) are labeled.

More tools (2026-10-16, creation corpus):

  • ebl_fetch.py (fixed again): a line with several variant reconstructions now prints all of them (N (variant, other manuscripts):) with their manuscripts; before, the second variant and its manuscripts were silently dropped. Re-run it on older eBL folders if a line looks incomplete.
  • Project-level verification pattern (סיפורי-הבריאה-המסופוטמיים/1-אנומה-אליש/verify.py): checks the annotated entries against eBL's line list, the translation lines against the annotated > lines, every pair of eBL "parallel lines" (bracket-only differences listed separately), and a fixed passage against its table in renderings.md. Copy and adapt it for any eBL-based multi-tablet project. The same folder has build_translation.py (one reading file from per-tablet files) and build_parallels_index.py (merges per-tablet parallels tables into the corpus parallels-index.md, ordered by verse).

More tools (2026-10-16, creation corpus project 2):

  • seal2md.py: a saved SEAL text page → Markdown (catalogue fields; the text table line by line, with bilingual continuation lines marked ↳; SEAL's per-word lemmas; the translation). python3 -I tools/seal2md.py <node-N.html> <out.md> <url>. SEAL returns an error page to curl's default User-Agent: download with a browser UA (see the docstring).
  • cdl2md.py --morph: the ORACC converter now prints each word's ePSD2 morph and base ({ba.n.da:~;a,bi.a;nud}), the Sumerian "check the stem" (§4.6).
  • check_bible_quotes.py (fixed 2026-10-17): the loose book key dropped every י and ו, so יהושע resolved to הושע; it now keeps the first letter and tries the exact name first.
  • eBL fragmentarium transliteration search: GET /api/fragments/query?transliteration=<signs> finds every fragment with a sign sequence (e.g. ul-le-gar-ra → VAT 9307 = KAR 4). Use it to look for duplicates of a text before declaring it single-manuscript.
  • Project-level verify.py for a multi-text project (סיפורי-הבריאה-המסופוטמיים/2-טקסטי-בריאה-ועדן/verify.py): per text, checks the annotated entries against the edition's line list (eBL reading edition or ETCSL transliteration) and the translation lines against the annotated > lines; build_translation.py there joins per-text files.

More tools (2026-10-17, law and treaty corpus):

  • cdl2md.py --norm: adds a norm: line (the project's normalization of each word; SAAo, RINAP etc.) and prints the contextual sense after the guide word ([(treaty-)oath=treaty]).

  • oracc_html2tr.py: a saved ORACC per-text HTML view → Markdown translation (units labelled with the transliteration lines they span, section headings as ##). python3 -I tools/oracc_html2tr.py <in.html> <out.md> <title> <url>. Use it for any ORACC project: the zips have no translations.

  • Project tools in חוקים-ובריתות/1-אמנת-הירושה-של-אסרחדון/: build_data.py + make_parts.py (align a composite with a later copy by the SAAo labels and cut per-part data files for the translators), verify.py (entries, one > per entry, reserved words, fixed formulas and key-lemma roots, identical normalizations), build_translation.py (clean translation with § headings and footnotes from a הערת שוליים field), build_parallels_index.py (corpus index, Deuteronomy grouped by chapter).

  • sources_sync.py (2026-10-21): re-obtains the git-ignored sources. status / fetch / verify (work tier by default; --all adds the archive tier of old scans and photos; --only REGEX, --dest DIR, --jobs N); snapshot rewrites sources/MANIFEST.json where the files are. The recipes are in sources/fetch-recipes.tsv. It reports CHANGED when an online edition changed since our copy, and names the hosts blocked by a cloud allowlist. Text files are compared with their "generated/retrieved" dates blanked. Never extracts .exe/.dll from a zip. snapshot in a partial checkout (a cloud session without the archive tier, or with files that are CHANGED) drops the absent items and re-stamps the changed ones: there, add only the new items to the committed manifest (as the lead did on 2026-10-21). On a certificate error it retries with the public intermediates in tools/certs/ (ORACC omits its intermediate; 2026-10-21), then falls back to curl with the same certificates.

When you write a tool that another session could reuse, put it here with a usage docstring and add a row to this table.

More tools (2026-10-17, the Laws of Hammurabi):

  • cdli_composite2md.py: a CDLI composite ATF with #tr.ts / #tr.en lines → Markdown, optionally aligned line by line with one witness ATF (stele/tablet) by the transliteration sequence, and a JSON-lines file. Get the ATF from https://cdli.earth/artifacts/<id>/json ([0]['inscription']['atf']; witnesses' ATF inside [0]['witnesses']). python3 -I tools/cdli_composite2md.py <composite.atf> <out.md> <title> <url> [--witness <w.atf> <siglum>] [--jsonl <out>].
  • Project tools in חוקים-ובריתות/2-חוקי-חמורבי/: lh_config.py (files, topics, composite parser, stele alignment, SEAL mapping), build_data.py (per-file translator data: composite + stele + SEAL lemmas + rank-3), verify.py (entries per file with placeholders, § sections against the composite, reserved words, formula patterns, identical normalizations, translation = > lines; --strict), build_translation.py (topic and § headings, footnotes, placeholders). Corpus builder חוקים-ובריתות/build_parallels_index.py merges every project's Part tables (Exodus and Deuteronomy by chapter); it replaces the project-1 builder.
  • check_bible_quotes.py (fixed 2026-10-17): references to דברי הימים א/ב were skipped; now matched.

More tools (2026-10-18, the other law collections, in חוקים-ובריתות/): laws_config.py (projects LE, MAL, MALB, LI, UN: CDLI composite parser with exemplar links, ORACC MAL parser with the § units of the translation, files, TOPICS; Hebrew helpers), laws_build_data.py KEY <dir> (translator data per file), laws_verify.py KEY [n…] [--strict] (entries, § ranges, reserved and lemma-gated words, LH's fixed formulas for Akkadian and their equivalents for Sumerian, identical normalizations inside and across collections, translation = > lines), laws_build_translation.py KEY (topic headings by § or by composite label @label), laws_lookup.py '<regex>' [--heb] [--proj …] (how LH and the new projects rendered a word); build_parallels_index.py now reads all seven projects. More tools (2026-10-19, creation corpus projects 3–4):

  • sumerian_workbench.py: the Sumerian workbench that project 2 asked for. lemmas <c.xml> FROM-TO (ETCSL's TEI lemmas per word), line <c.xml> FROM-TO (the same, plus for every verb the ORACC morph of the same form wherever it is parsed in epsd2-literary, or "no parsed instance: our analysis"), morph '<form>', conc '<regex>' [--lemma] (ETCSL-wide concordance, for formulas), gloss '<regex>' (ePSD2 glossary). The ORACC form index is built once into sources/ORACC/_bulk/epsd2-literary--form-index.json (gitignored). Run with python3 -I.
  • סיפורי-הבריאה-המסופוטמיים/sumerian_tools.py: verify KEY [--strict] (coverage against the ETCSL line list over several annotated files, one > per entry, reserved strings licensed by the Sumerian word, name traps, identical transliterations with different Hebrew), build KEY (the clean translation generated from translation--intro.rtl.md + the annotated ## headings and > lines, with הערת שוליים bullets as footnotes), grep all '<regex>' (projects 2–7). Add a project as a PROJECTS entry. With translator-brief--sumerian.md (the reusable brief). 1-אנומה-אליש/build_parallels_index.py reads projects 3–7 (sigla B&F, EWO, FI, H&P, S&W). Since 2026-10-22 (Round 3 run 1): projects 5–7 (gates57) add RESERVED_5_7 (substring gates) and TOKEN_GATES_5_7 (whole-word gates: each Hebrew token is tried with every prefix split – ו, ה, ב, ל, מ, כ, ש and pairs – and needs the licensing Sumerian word; TOKEN_EXEMPT_5_7 lists ordinary words a split would turn into a gated one, e.g. בקר, לחם, מעצב, מנחה); the Sumer / Urim name traps; the עבד gate also licensed by arad; brackets are stripped from both the Hebrew and the transliteration before every gate (a half-bracketed word, ק[יץ], is read whole). Run brief: translator-brief--sumerian--5-7.md with …--shared-lemmas.txt.

More tools (2026-10-19, the wisdom corpus, in ספרות-החכמה-והצדיק-הסובל/): wisdom_config.py (files with eBL line ranges, so one eBL chapter can be split over several annotated files; eBL readers; the Gilgameš corpus's Hebrew for cross-corpus parallels) and wisdom_tools.py – pars KEY (eBL parallels incl. cross-text L I.4 links to Gilgameš, and identical normalizations, with the Hebrew already given), verify [KEY…] [--strict] (entries, translation = > lines, reserved strings licensed by an eBL lemma or a normalization token, vocalization traps gated by lemma, repeated lines), build (per-file and per-project clean translations generated from translation--intro-<KEY>.rtl.md + the annotated file; never edited by hand), grep '<regex>' [--gilg], lemma '<regex>' (how a lemma was rendered so far: the cheapest consistency tool); build_parallels_index.py (Job first, then Psalms, Qohelet, Proverbs, Lamentations, Isaiah, Jeremiah, the Torah). translator-brief.md there is the reusable brief for Akkadian eBL texts.

More tools (2026-10-19, the city-lament corpus, in קינות-על-ערים/): lament_tools.py – verify KEY [--strict] (entries against the ETCSL line list with segment labels A1… for fragmentary segments, the backticked transliteration equal to ETCSL's line, reserved and gated strings licensed by a Sumerian word, name traps, fixed refrains checked by regex (FORMULAS), translation = > lines, identical lines with different Hebrew), build KEY, grep KEY|all (this corpus + the creation corpus's Sumerian texts), lines KEY FROM-TO (ETCSL's lines for a brief); build_parallels_index.py (Lamentations first, then Psalms, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Isaiah, the other Prophets, the Torah, Daniel); translator-brief--laments.md (the reusable brief for Sumerian liturgical texts). Add a project as a PROJECTS entry.

More tools (2026-10-20, the temple-building corpus, in בניין-המקדש/): temple_tools.py – conc GU [<out>] (the label concordance: ETCSL composite numbers ↔ RIME column-line labels ↔ ORACC, with a per-line similarity check), data GU FROM TO <out> (a translator's line-data file: ETCSL transliteration, ORACC lemma + morph, and the two rank-3 translations – ETCSL's paragraphs mapped from composite numbers to labels, ETCSRI's units – at their first line), verify GU [--strict] (as lament_tools.py, for labels A.ix.10; the reserved Tabernacle words and the gated building words), build GU, grep GU|all, lines; build_parallels_index.py (Exodus first, then Kings, Chronicles, Ezekiel, Genesis …); translator-brief--temple.md (the reusable brief for Sumerian royal and building texts). More tools (2026-10-21, the netherworld corpus, in העולם-התחתון/): netherworld_tools.py – verify IS|IN [--strict] (entries vs. the eBL labels incl. NA1… and the ETCSL labels; the backticked source = the base text; reserved and gated Hebrew licensed by the eBL normalization/lemma or the Sumerian word; name traps; fixed formulas, also across the two languages; translation = > lines; identical sources with different Hebrew), build IS|IN, lines IS|IN FROM TO (base lines with eBL lemmas / ORACC lemma + morph), grep all '<regex>' (the > lines of every corpus, niqqud stripped); build_parallels_index.py – generates the per-project parallels tables from the annotated הקבלה bullets and merges them by Bible verse into parallels-index.md (the key findings kept): no hand-copied tables, so the index cannot drift from the annotations; recommended for new corpora.

More tools (2026-10-22, the netherworld corpus, Round 3 run 5): netherworld_tools.py now has keys NE (Nergal and Ereškigal: two eBL chapters, the MB labelled MB.<label>, then the SB) and GEN (Bilgameš, Enkidu and the Netherworld: an ETCSL composite with several recensions – versions=[(heading, prefix)] gives each bold version heading of transliteration.md its own label prefix, U58., U59.A…, MT.B…; ORACC aligned by position, now also with labels like Ver.1, 12); xii FROM TO prints each Sumerian line with its Gilgameš XII counterparts and their Hebrew (XII_CONC, aligned by content and corrected by the translators: George's "BN" numbers run ~1 ahead of ETCSL) – the pattern for any Sumerian text with an ancient Akkadian translation already translated; new reserved / gated words (סולם, מלאך, לילית, בדל, רקיע; גן by kiri₆, פוכו, היכל), traps (Anu אָנוּ, Kakka כַּכָּה, Erra אֶרָּה, pukku, mekkû, eṭemmu אִט, Sumer שׁוּמֶר) and formulas for both texts. Fixed: variant parentheses (1 ms. has instead: …) are removed before the italic notes (their words leaked into the formula check); ⸢ ⸣ are removed before the formula check; the gate licences read eBL's h as ḫ; a heading with a single label (## b+50: …) is stripped in build. build_parallels_index.py reads projects 3–4 and skips missing files.

More tools (2026-10-21, the legends-of-kings corpus, in אגדות-מלכים/; run with python3 -I -B): kings_tools.py – verify EA|SB [--strict] (entries vs. the base line list: ETCSL 1.8.2.3, King 1907 labels I.n / II.n; transliteration = base text; reserved and gated strings tested on the transliteration with and without brackets; name traps in lines and headings; fixed formulas; translation = > lines; identical transliterations with different Hebrew), build EA|SB, grep EA|SB|all, lines, pars KEY FROM TO (each line's earlier copies, ratio ≥ 0.75, with their Hebrew: for command/delivery texts), conc EA (ETCSL ↔ ORACC Q000369, whose variant lines are unlabelled), data EA FROM TO out (a translator's data file with ETCSL, ORACC lemma + morph, ETCSL's English and Mittermayer's German from the OCR); build_parallels_index.py (Genesis first, then Exodus).

More tools (2026-10-21, the everyday-voices corpus, in קולות-היום-יום/): kol_tools.py – units; data UNIT [FROM [TO]] (a translator's line data: label, transliteration, normalization, lemmas + ORACC morph, the rank-3 translation; per proverb for the proverbs); fill FILE (replaces each `@` transliteration placeholder by the exact base line: drafting with @ removed every retyping mismatch – recommended for every corpus); verify [UNIT|PROJECT …] [--strict] (coverage and order, transliteration = base, reserved and gated strings licensed by the line's transliteration + normalization + lemmas, anchored at word start, name traps, formulas, identical sources with different Hebrew, translation = > lines); build PROJECT; grep (PROJECT|all|every) '<regex>'; lookup '<regex>' (how the earlier corpora rendered a word); build_parallels_index.py [--stats] – generates parallels-index.md straight from the annotated הקבלה bullets (no per-project tables), grouped by book with the Song of Songs, Proverbs and Qohelet first, keeping the hand-written key findings.

  • ebl_fetch.py (fixed 2026-10-22, Etana): a reconstruction line that opens with a logogram in another language (25. %sb U₄.1.KAM@v.TA.AM₃ | %n inaṣṣarū …) was not recognized (only %n was), so it was glued to the previous line as a "variant" and its own N was empty. Now any %<language> opening is a reconstruction line, and the language markers are dropped from N. Re-run the tool on an older eBL folder if a line has an empty N.
  • ebl_fetch.py (2026-10-21, Round 3 run 5): prints every non-English translation too, as T (de): (eBL's Nergal and Ereškigal MB has only Mitto's German; before, the chapter looked untranslated). Re-run it on an older eBL folder to add the German where eBL has it (no normalization changes).

  • tools/harmonize_survey.py (2026-10-23, the post-Round-3 harmonization): which Hebrew each corpus uses for a source word, across every annotated*.rtl.md of the folder. src REGEX [--heb REGEX] [--show N] (entries whose transliteration or parse names the source word, per project; with --heb, split by whether the > line has the Hebrew); heb REGEX [--src REGEX] (entries whose > line has the Hebrew, niqqud stripped; with --src, the collisions: the same Hebrew for another source word); words REGEX (the Hebrew words of the matching entries, counted); parse REGEX (the parse segments that name the word: note that their quoted glosses are dictionary meanings, not always the chosen Hebrew). Anchor Hebrew regexes at word start and end ((^|[^א-ת])ו?[בלכמהש]?(…)). Run with python3 -I.

More tools (2026-10-21, printed rows; moved 2026-10-24): layout/rows-tool.ts – measures, proposes and checks the printed rows of a translation.rtl.md (its translation.rtl.layout.ts, through layout/translation-layout.ts - the translations' layout logic, beside it), in the same Chromium, fonts and A4 width as the PDF printer. It never writes the module: try and propose print the row starts as constants to put into it. bun layout/rows-tool.ts status | report <file> [--text] [--widths] [--run=N] [--review] | try <file> --run=N --move=a>b | propose <file> [--fix] | check <file> | resolve <file> | template <file> [--rules] | compare <file> --with=<module> | md5 <file> | preview <file> --pages=2-4,9 --out=<dir>, and --layout=<module> / --out=<path>. bun run layout-status (in _RTL-EDITOR) lists every file whose layout is missing, obsolete (the file changed since), flagged or broken. Used by layout sessions; see layout/layout-guidelines.md §3.
